ios.desc:
Am I Secure? performs forensic analysis of your iPhone or iPad to find signs of compromise. If you are a journalist, activist, executive, lawyer, government official or anyone with reason to think you may be of interest to a sophisticated adversary, this app is built for you. The same applies if you hold digital assets in self-custody. The device holding your keys is the target, and that device is what Am I Secure? examines.

WHAT A COMPROMISED DEVICE MEANS
Your whole life is on your phone. Private messages, email, photos, contacts, financial information. If you can read it, so can someone who has compromised the device. Encryption protects your messages in transit; it does not protect anything once the device itself is under someone else's control. An attacker in that position can read your messages before they are encrypted and after they are decrypted, see your location, take your stored credentials, and reach any account you are signed in to. They can listen through the microphone to conversations in the room, record through the camera, and follow your movements. There is generally no way to tell from using the device.

WHY THIS REQUIRES A DIFFERENT APPROACH
iOS is among the most secure consumer platforms available. iOS does not let any app, including security apps, look outside its own container or "sandbox". No security app on your device can inspect the processes, the filesystem, or the behavior of the rest of the system. That is a deliberate security property of the platform, and it is why an app running on your phone can only report on your settings, not on what is actually running.

Am I Secure? works differently. You generate a system diagnostic "sysdiagnose" file using the tool built into iOS. That file is produced by the operating system itself, not by us, and it contains a detailed record of processes, logs, and system state. You share that file with the app, which uploads it to our servers. We analyze it and report what we find.

The diagnostic file is end-to-end encrypted on your device before it is uploaded and stays encrypted until it reaches hardware we own and operate in our own facilities in Canada and the European Union (EU). It is not decrypted or accessible by any third party, including intermediary data center and network operators. Once analysis is complete the file is deleted.

A HUMAN REVIEWS ANYTHING UNUSUAL
Where our automated analysis flags something, our team examines the results by hand before anything is reported to you. T

quotes.text:
Background
In 2021, my iPhone was exploited with spyware (Pegasus) by a client of the NSO Group due to my employment at the time (i.e. I worked for a target organization). From there I began helping other at risk users identify when their iPhones were compromised via manual forensic analysis of their devices. Wanted to scale this manual forensic analysis to a wider audience to make it widely available to find more victims of spyware companies like NSO Group (Pegasus) and Cytrox (Predator) so created an app to do it called Am I Secure? that is on the App Store now. It is able to detect the latest variants of spyware (including those deployed against victims in April 2024). The app also performs a number of other security checks, more than any other iOS app.

Key Differentiator
All iOS apps operate within an "app sandbox", a restricted space within iOS that limits an app to accessing only its own data and specific data a user has provided permission to, such as contacts or location data. This is to ensure security and privacy. Due to these restrictions, no iOS apps, including security focussed ones, are able to directly access the operating system and other data necessary to perform an analysis of the operating system for spyware or malware.
